title: Day Trading: Opening Range, VWAP & Scalps
subtitle: Intraday structure, the opening range, VWAP and scalping mechanics, tested on 60 real SPY sessions, with the costs and base rates that decide whether any of it pays.
what_you_learn: The published base rates for retail day traders, the intraday margin standard that replaced the pattern-day-trader rule in 2026, and how to read a 60-trade result with a confidence interval
Where volume and range live inside the session, measured from 60 real SPY sessions, and why the same dollar stop means different things at 09:35 and 12:30
The opening-range breakout defined precisely enough to test, with a 60-session result for twelve variants, an in-sample versus out-of-sample split, and what that split says about picking rules
VWAP as a benchmark and as a reference: how to compute it by hand, how often price reverts to it, and a tested pullback entry that lost money on the sample
Why round-trip cost as a share of risk decides whether scalping can work, why level 2 and the tape cannot tell you what people assume, and what a 0DTE version of the opening range does at 16:00
A one-setup playbook with stop-based sizing, a daily loss limit, time stops and a fourteen-field journal, and a 30-session capstone graded on the honesty of the evidence rather than its sign
